0-1.site: Retract Reef overworld: Landing Pier → the Walkway, the Fork, the O, Twin Lagoons → Null's Mirage at the broken causeway.
0-1.story: Morning after the collapse. Gyroid wakes at the Landing Pier; the walkway slabs are gone but the amber spines held. Emmy shows how a thick reef shrinks onto its spine without losing anything that matters. With four reefs saved, Null's Mirage stages four forged 'retractions'; naming the broken rule in each mends the causeway to Tidewarp Flats.
0-1.objective: Save the four reefs by shrinking each onto a spine through its beacons, then expose Null's four forgeries.
mechanics: Explore in third person (WASD); overhead follow camera; minimap from the World 0 map.
Fundamental Lash (click toward the mouse): spheres collapse in one lash, tori need two (one loop each).
Spool (2 / Q, click to start and stop): walk to lay spine thread on a reef.
Slide: the reef deformation-retracts onto the spine; Gyroid rides his own tile. Saved reefs regrow, healed.
The spine is valid when it is connected and every region of reef − spine touches exactly one shore; otherwise the failing region turns red with a diagnosis (leak / fenced patch / disconnected).
0-1.math_check: Deformation retraction of a planar region onto a drawn graph: valid iff the spine is connected and each complementary region is a collar on a single boundary curve; the slide follows the gradient of a harmonic function in each collar (continuous by construction).

stages.name: The Walkway
stages.description: Clear two spheres; the spine is given; watch the slide and the five rules turn green.

stages.name: The Fork
stages.description: A thick T: spool a spine through three beacons.

stages.name: The O
stages.description: First torus. A short spine leaks across the ring; only a loop around the hole holds.

stages.name: Twin Lagoons
stages.description: A disk with two holes: figure-eight, theta or barbell spines all work (Hatcher's three).

stages.name: Null's Mirage
stages.description: Four forgeries, each breaking one rule; name the rule. Wins mend the broken causeway.

enemies.name: Sphere spawn
enemies.description: One lash; loops slide off a sphere, so it collapses to a point.

enemies.name: Torus spawn
enemies.description: Two lashes: the first lights a loop around its tube, the second a loop through its hole.

0-1.tools: Uses the Lash; unlocks the Spool (anchor_spool).
0-1.music: The Retract Reef theme: 92 bpm D dorian chiptune — pads, echoing pulse arpeggio, triangle bass, sine lead on the second phrase.
0-1.visuals: Basalt reefs on a dark luminous sea, gold spines and beacons, violet spawn; saved reefs warm to a pale gold-grey.

0-2.site: Tidewarp Flats — wide wet basalt flats east of the mended causeway, with tide pools and stone posts.
0-2.story: Past the mended causeway the tide reshapes every path on the flats each hour. Null's engineers 'help' by snapping paths straight to a single post. Gyroid learns that a homotopy is the whole continuous movie of maps — and that a snap is not a movie.
0-2.objective: Guide the tide: deform gold ribbon-paths into the shapes the shrines ask for, keeping the marked posts fixed, without crossing open water.
mechanics: Ribbons are maps from an interval into the flats. Gyroid grabs a ribbon point with the Spool and walks it; the ribbon bends continuously behind him (a homotopy, recorded as a ghost trail).
Posts pin points of a ribbon: a homotopy rel those posts never moves them.
Tide pools are holes in the flats: a ribbon can't pass through water, so some targets can only be reached by going around.
Tide Glass (new): scrub a recorded deformation backwards and forwards in time — every frame must connect to the next.
Null's Snap: a ‘deformation’ that jumps; the player finds the frame where it tears.
0-2.math_check: Path homotopy in a planar region with holes, rel endpoints; continuity in time (consecutive frames are close); retraction (a single map) versus deformation retraction (a continuous family).

stages.name: Tide Line
stages.description: The tide bends a ribbon on its own; scrub the Tide Glass and watch a homotopy as a movie of maps.

stages.name: Hold the Posts
stages.description: Walk a ribbon into the shrine's target shape with both end posts fixed — a homotopy rel endpoints.

stages.name: The Pools
stages.description: Two targets on opposite sides of a tide pool: one is reachable by sliding around the pool, the other isn't by any slide Gyroid can find. Emmy: proving it's impossible needs a tool from the next world.

stages.name: Null's Snap
stages.description: Null retracts the whole flats onto one post in a single snap. Every space retracts to a point; find the frame where his ‘deformation’ tears.

enemies.name: Snapper
enemies.description: New: a violet crab that clips ribbons. A clipped ribbon is discontinuous and must be re-tied before the shrine accepts it. One lash.

enemies.name: Sphere and torus spawn
enemies.description: As in 0-1, now drifting with the tide.

0-2.tools: Uses the Lash and Spool; unlocks the Tide Glass (scrub time).
0-2.music: Variation on the reef theme: slower (80 bpm), tidal swells on the pad, a ticking clock-like pluck when the Tide Glass is out.
0-2.visuals: Mirror-wet basalt flats at low tide, stone posts, glowing gold ribbons with translucent ghost copies; violet sparks where a snap tears.

0-3.site: Mirror Shoals — five reefs on either side of a glassy, star-reflecting channel: Solid Shoal, Ring Reef, Twin Mirror, the Dumbbell, and the reef before the Mirror Gate to the Skeleton Foundry.
0-3.story: The figure-eight and the theta both came from Twin Lagoons, yet they look nothing alike. Emmy shows how to prove two places are 'the same shape': maps both ways whose round trips slide home. The Mirror Gate opens only for someone who can do it — and Emmy seems to know what's behind it.
0-3.objective: Prove reefs are the same shape: shrink loops, slide reefs onto spines (0-1's deformation retraction), and show one reef slides onto two different spines — then open the Mirror Gate.
mechanics: Loops on stakes (0-2's Spool): unhook every stake and a loop on solid ground shrinks to its post; around a hole it catches.
Point spine: a one-point spine slides a solid reef onto a point — contractible (homotopy equivalent to a point).

Two spines, one reef: the same two-hole reef deformation retracts onto a figure-eight and onto a theta, so they are homotopy equivalent (Hatcher, Corollary 0.21: both are deformation retracts of one space).
One loop per hole: a ring spine on a two-hole reef leaks; adding a second loop and a bar (a barbell) works.
Mirror spawn: each has an intangible reflection across its reef's mirror line; only the solid one can be lashed.
The lesson shows explicit maps f : eight → theta and g : theta → eight (collapse the bar) whose round trips slide home.
0-3.math_check: Homotopy equivalence (fg ≃ 1, gf ≃ 1) and contractibility (Hatcher pp. 3–4), proved in play via deformation retractions checked by the 0-1 slide engine; X ≃ Y iff both are deformation retracts of some Z (Corollary 0.21, p. 16). Flag: that the ring is not contractible is left unproved until World 1.

stages.name: Solid Shoal
stages.description: Unhook a loop: it shrinks to its post. Then a one-point spine slides the whole reef onto a point — contractible.

stages.name: Ring Reef
stages.description: Its loop catches on the hole; Emmy flags that proving it can't shrink needs World 1.

stages.name: Twin Mirror
stages.description: Slide one two-hole reef onto a figure-eight, let it regrow, then onto a theta: the two spines are the same shape.

stages.name: Dumbbell
stages.description: Null's ring spine leaks (a hole without a loop); a barbell spine works.

stages.name: The Mirror Gate
stages.description: Any valid spine on an odd two-hole reef; the gate lights figure-eight, theta and barbell, leaves the ring dark, and opens onto the Foundry.

enemies.name: Mirror spawn
enemies.description: New: a faceted mirror-crystal creature with an intangible, flickering reflection across its reef's mirror line; lash the solid one. One lash.

0-3.tools: Uses the Lash and Spool (spines and loops).
0-3.music: Mirror Shoals theme: 72 bpm E lydian celesta bells over a slow pad; every two-bar motif is answered by its mirror image (inverted).
0-3.visuals: A still mirror channel reflecting stars; two thick basalt reefs; gold threads arcing between them; a tall mirrored gate with forge-light behind it.
0-3.movie: level-0-3-intro “Two Reefs, One Shape” and the lesson level-0-3-lesson “Same Shape”.

0-4.site: The Skeleton Foundry's Assembly Hall — four forge stations (round basalt platforms with a furnace hub and petal tracks) under a press gantry, and the forge door to the Cone Zone.
0-4.story: Through the Mirror Gate, Emmy's secret comes out: she built the Foundry's cell presses, and Null's engineers turned them into collapse engines. She gives Gyroid the Cell-Smith so they can build places back — cell by cell.
0-4.objective: Forge cell complexes at four presses — the sphere (twice), the torus, the projective plane and the Klein bottle — and open the forge door with χ.
mechanics: Cell-Smith (new): click the furnace hub to forge the point (the one 0-cell).
Walk a petal track out from the hub and back: an edge (a 1-cell), a loop at the point, arrow in the direction walked, lettered a, b.
Walk a word along the edges (forward = a, against the arrow = a⁻¹), then click the hub: the press glues a disk (a 2-cell) along that loop.
The press's hologram folds the flat cell into the space it makes; a wrong word builds something else, shown and explained, then let go.
χ = points − edges + disks, counted live on the blueprint card.
Unglues tear forged edges; re-walk a torn track to re-forge it.
0-4.math_check: Cell complexes built skeleton by skeleton (Hatcher pp. 5–8); one-vertex structures: S² = e⁰ ∪ e² and also e⁰ ∪ e¹ ∪ 2e²; T² along a b a⁻¹ b⁻¹; RP² along a a; Klein bottle along a b a⁻¹ b; χ as even minus odd cells (Example 0.2). Flag: that χ depends only on the space is Theorem 2.44 (Chapter 2) — stated, not proved here. Also: with one vertex, a disk on a a⁻¹ is a sphere with two points glued (χ = 1), and the game says so.

stages.name: The Sphere Press
stages.description: Point + a disk with its rim crushed to it: a sphere. Again as one edge + two hemispheres: same χ = 2.

stages.name: Twin Loops
stages.description: Edges a, b; a disk along a b a⁻¹ b⁻¹: the torus folds (roll, then bend). χ = 0.

stages.name: One Loop
stages.description: A disk along a just fills the loop (a disk); along a a it's the projective plane, which crosses itself in 3D.

stages.name: The Blueprint Wall
stages.description: a b a⁻¹ b under an Unglue wave: the Klein bottle; then answer χ = 0 to open the forge door.

enemies.name: Unglue
enemies.description: New: a violet seam-ripper that tears forged edges loose; re-walk the track to re-forge. One lash.

0-4.music: Forge theme: 100 bpm C minor — anvil strikes on the off-beats, square bass and brass, bellows swells, the reef melody in minor.
0-4.visuals: Basalt forge hall, furnaces glowing amber, cranes laying curved glowing edges, a square sheet folding into a torus mid-air; Gyroid's brass-and-indigo gauntlet.
0-4.movie: level-0-4-intro “Emmy's Foundry” and the lesson level-0-4-lesson “Built from Cells”.

0-5.site: Cone Zone — a terrace of workstations on the Foundry cliff.
0-5.story: Null's engineers are 'fixing' ring islands by coning them off: joining every point of a ring to one tip, which fills the hole. Gyroid learns the operations on spaces — cone, suspension, wedge, product, quotient — so a plugged hole can't fool him.
0-5.objective: Stop the coning crews and use the stations to build target spaces from simpler ones.
mechanics: Operation stations: feed a space in, choose cone, suspension, wedge or product, and get the new space (with its cells added).
Recipe puzzles: reach a target space by a chain of operations (circle → suspension → sphere; circle × circle → torus; circle ∨ circle → figure-eight).
Quotients: collapse a subspace to a point; collapsing something contractible keeps the shape, collapsing a loop doesn't.
Spot the plug: a coned ring is a disk — contractible — even if it still looks like a ring from the side.
0-5.math_check: Cones are contractible; suspension of Sⁿ is Sⁿ⁺¹; products and wedges add cells predictably; collapsing a contractible subcomplex preserves homotopy type.

stages.name: The Cone
stages.description: Watch a crew cone a ring: the hole fills. Any cone shrinks to its tip.

stages.name: Two Tips
stages.description: Suspend two points: a circle. Suspend a circle: a sphere.

stages.name: Wedge and Product
stages.description: Build the figure-eight as a wedge and the torus as circle × circle; compare it with the torus from the Assembly Hall by counting cells.

stages.name: Recipes
stages.description: Chain operations to match three targets while coning crews try to plug your inputs.

enemies.name: Coner
enemies.description: New: a violet engineer drone that beams a cone onto a ring; lash it before the beam finishes or the ring is plugged. Two lashes.

0-5.tools: Uses the Cell-Smith; unlocks the Suspension Sling (suspension_sling).
0-5.music: Bright, mechanical: arpeggios that climb and fold back (cone up, cone down), a steady four-on-the-floor kick.
0-5.visuals: Terraced basalt stations under moonlight, glowing gold cones and double cones, a small circle sweeping a torus; violet drones with cone beams.
0-5.movie: level-0-5-intro “Null's Plugs” and the lesson level-0-5-lesson “New Spaces from Old”.

0-6.site: Timber Yard — a tangled network of narrow walkways over the sea at the Foundry's edge; the unbuilt bridge to the Hollow Throne starts here.
0-6.story: The yard's walkways have grown into a tangle. Felling a tree of walkways keeps the shape; felling a loop erases a hole — which is exactly what Null's spawn do. Counting platforms minus walkways tells bouquets apart. With the yard cleared, Gyroid forges the bridge to the Throne.
0-6.objective: Collapse each tangle to a bouquet of loops without killing a loop, and read its petal count from χ.
mechanics: Mark a tree with the Spool: amber walkways that reach every platform without closing a loop.
Fell: tree walkways fold toward one platform; the rest become petals of a bouquet.
Loop guard: trying to fell a walkway whose ends are the same platform is refused (it would erase a hole).
Census: χ = platforms − walkways never changes when a tree is felled; petals = 1 − χ.
Bridge: after the census, forge the Throne bridge's cells with the Cell-Smith.
0-6.math_check: Collapsing a contractible subcomplex (a tree) is a homotopy equivalence; every connected graph is ≃ a wedge of 1 − χ circles.

stages.name: One Edge
stages.description: Shrink a single walkway between two platforms: nothing is lost.

stages.name: Spanning Tree
stages.description: Mark a tree that touches every platform; fell it; count the petals.

stages.name: The Wrong Cut
stages.description: Loop-biter spawn collapse a petal; stop them, and see why a loop can't be felled.

stages.name: Census
stages.description: Three tangles that look different: fell all three and sort them by χ.

enemies.name: Loop-biter
enemies.description: New: violet beetles that chew a petal loop and collapse it. Two lashes.

0-6.music: Woodwind-like square leads and a log-drum pattern; a big chord on each successful fell.
0-6.visuals: A web of narrow basalt walkways, a highlighted amber tree folding inward, petals of a bouquet around one glowing node; the black spire across the water.
0-6.movie: level-0-6-intro “Timber Yard” and the lesson level-0-6-lesson “Felling Trees”.

0-B.site: Cylinder Works — a sealed workshop off the Assembly Hall holding a huge translucent cylinder.
0-B.story: Emmy's first machine. If you already know how the edge of a piece moves, can you extend that motion over the whole piece without changing where it starts? For anything built from cells, yes — one cell at a time.
0-B.objective: Fill the cylinder's interior with a motion that matches the given floor and side band, cell by cell.
mechanics: The floor shows the starting map; a band on the side shows the prescribed motion of a subcomplex.
Extend cell by cell with the Cell-Smith, in order of dimension: points, then edges, then disks.
A cell can be filled only once the motion on its boundary is already decided.
0-B.math_check: The homotopy extension property for CW pairs: X×{0} ∪ A×I is a retract of X×I, built cell by cell.

stages.name: Floor and Band
stages.description: Read the start and the prescribed motion.

stages.name: Points First
stages.description: Extend over the 0-cells, then the edges.

stages.name: Wrong Order
stages.description: Try a disk before its edges: refused.

stages.name: Full Cylinder
stages.description: Fill the whole interior.

0-B.music: A music-box version of the forge theme, sparse and warm.
0-B.visuals: A tall translucent cylinder filling with gold light cell by cell; an arched window onto the moonlit sea.
0-B.movie: level-0-b-intro “The Cylinder Works” and the lesson level-0-b-lesson “One Cell at a Time”.

castle.site: The Hollow Throne — Null's black-glass spire in the northwest, reached over the bridge forged at the Timber Yard.
castle.story: Gyroid climbs to Null's throne room, where the Null Crown hangs over a floor of shifting reef. Null tests everything World 0 taught: fake deformations, illegal collapses, false equivalences. Gyroid beats every forgery — but when Null insists a ring is secretly a point, Gyroid has no proof. Null laughs and escapes along the broken Winding Way.
castle.objective: Survive Null's three trials and expose every illegal simplification.

phases.name: Live forgeries
phases.description: Null's deformations play out on the arena floor. Lash the frame where a rule breaks (starts still, stays on the reef, ends on the spine, spine fixed, no tearing) to freeze it. Tests 0-1 and 0-2.

phases.name: Simplifications
phases.description: Null collapses three walkway networks. Lash the beacons of illegal collapses (a loop felled, a hole coned) and spare the legal ones (a tree felled). Tests 0-5 and 0-6.

phases.name: Same shape?
phases.description: Null shows pairs of reefs and claims they match. Build the round-trip maps for the true pairs; refuse the false ones. Tests 0-3.

phases.name: The ring
phases.description: Null holds up a ring: ‘It's just a point.’ No World 0 tool can refute him — the arena's rules all hold for every slide Gyroid tries. Null escapes. Scripted loss of the argument, win of the castle.

enemies.name: Crown shards
enemies.description: Violet fragments orbiting Null that dive at Gyroid; one lash each.

enemies.name: Every World 0 spawn
enemies.description: Waves of spheres, tori, Snappers, Coners and Loop-biters between phases.

castle.tools: Everything from World 0: Lash, Spool, Tide Glass, Cell-Smith, Suspension Sling.
castle.music: Null's motif (D–E♭–D–A) on a pipe-organ-like square pad, rising a semitone each phase; the reef theme returns in a minor key when Null escapes.
castle.visuals: A circular throne room of black glass at the top of the spire, the Null Crown floating above, a reef-tile floor that ripples with Null's deformations, the moonlit world far below through open arches.
castle.movie: castle-0-intro “The Hollow Throne” and castle-0-outro “A Ring Is a Ring”.

castle_art.scene: Castle 'The Hollow Throne': a circular throne room of black glass at the top of a tall black spire, open arches looking down on a moonlit archipelago far below. The floor is made of basalt reef tiles rippling as if being deformed. Above an empty obsidian throne floats a broken circular crown of black metal with violet inward-pointing spikes, glowing violet. Count Null (tall, obsidian robes, pale porcelain mask, from the reference) stands before the throne holding up a glowing ring. Gyroid stands facing him across the floor with a gold lasso. Violet crown shards orbit the room.

videos.title: The Hollow Throne
videos.plays: Before castle-0, after crossing the forged bridge from the Timber Yard
videos.synopsis: Gyroid crosses the bridge forged at the Timber Yard and climbs the black spire. In the throne room Null waits under the Crown, amused that a courier has come to argue shapes with him. He promises three trials.

scenes.title: The bridge
scenes.description: Gyroid runs across the newly forged gold-seamed bridge toward the black spire; the Foundry glows behind. Emmy stays at the bridgehead.

scenes.title: The climb
scenes.description: A spiral stair of black glass around the spire's outside; the world falls away below.

scenes.title: The throne room
scenes.description: A circular hall with open arches. The reef-tile floor ripples. Null stands before an empty throne, the Crown floating overhead.

scenes.title: Three trials
scenes.description: Null gestures; three violet sigils light in the floor. Crown shards begin to orbit.

scenes.title: Title
scenes.description: Title card at 30: “World 0 · Castle — The Hollow Throne”.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: The bridge holds. Go — I'll keep the Foundry lit behind you.

captions.speaker: Narrator
captions.text: The Hollow Throne: a spire of black glass, and at its top, the one who started the collapse.

captions.speaker: Count Null
captions.text: The courier who keeps holes. You've learned to bend my reef without breaking it. Impressive.

captions.speaker: Count Null
captions.text: But bending is cheap. Can you tell a true simplification from a false one?

captions.speaker: Count Null
captions.text: Three trials. Fail one, and your precious reef becomes a point.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: Then I won't fail.

videos.title: A Ring Is a Ring
videos.plays: After castle-0's final phase — the end of World 0
videos.synopsis: Gyroid has exposed every forgery. Null holds up a ring and calls it a point; Gyroid can't prove otherwise. Null escapes along the severed Winding Way toward Bouquet Bastion. Emmy names what they need: an invariant.

scenes.title: The last claim
scenes.description: The arena still. Null lifts a glowing ring between two fingers.

scenes.title: No proof
scenes.description: Gyroid tries to slide the ring to a point on the arena floor; every slide stops short of the hole. He can't make it shrink — but he can't show it never could.

scenes.title: Escape
scenes.description: Null steps backwards off the spire's edge onto a violet ribbon of light that races away north along the broken Way.

scenes.title: Emmy
scenes.description: At the bridgehead at dawn, Emmy and Gyroid look north: the Way's next stretch leads to two loop districts meeting at a beacon.

scenes.title: World 0 complete
scenes.description: Card: “World 0 complete — Retract Reef restored.” Then the World 1 map unfolds.

captions.speaker: Count Null
captions.text: Every trick of mine, exposed. Well done. Now — this ring.

captions.speaker: Count Null
captions.text: It is a point. Prove it isn't.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: Every slide I try stops at the hole. It won't shrink.

captions.speaker: Count Null
captions.text: Won't — or can't? You don't know. Nobody here knows.

captions.speaker: Narrator
captions.text: And with that, Null stepped off the spire and was gone up the broken Winding Way.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: He's right about one thing. Bending can't prove a hole is there. We need something that counts it.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: Then we follow him, and find it.

videos.title: How the Tide Works
videos.plays: After the 0-2 intro, before play starts; replayable from the level's “How it works” button
videos.synopsis: A slowed-down explainer of 0-2's idea and tools. A path is a map f : I → X; a homotopy is a continuous movie of paths, one map F on the square I × I whose rows are the frames fₜ; rel A means the posts never move (the square's side edges). The Tide Glass scrubs t; the Spool makes homotopies by hand and hooks the ribbon onto stakes. What breaks a homotopy: a cut, a jump between frames, crossing water. A 3D demo on the flats plays beside a 2D diagram of the interval and the square.

scenes.title: A path is a map
scenes.description: Top-down over a ribbon between two posts. A bead slides along the ribbon while, in the diagram, a bead slides along the interval [0, 1]: s ↦ f(s).

scenes.title: A homotopy is a movie
scenes.description: The tide bends the ribbon from t = 0 to t = 1; five frames freeze as ghosts. The diagram becomes the square I × I, each frozen frame a row, the current frame a gold row at height t.

scenes.title: The Tide Glass
scenes.description: The movie scrubs back and forth; the diagram shows the Tide Glass slider and Z / X keys, and faint ghosts hug the ribbon on either side.

scenes.title: Rel A
scenes.description: The two posts pulse gold; the square's left and right edges light up: F(0, t) = a, F(1, t) = b for every t — the ribbon's ends are pinned (A).

scenes.title: The Spool
scenes.description: Gyroid walks to the ribbon, clicks to grab it, walks it out to a stake and clicks to let go; it hooks on. The diagram lights each control as it's used.

scenes.title: What breaks a homotopy
scenes.description: Three forbidden moves: a cut (the ribbon in two pieces, violet sparks), a jump (two neighbouring frames far apart), and crossing water at the pool shrine (the wet stretch violet).

scenes.title: Summary
scenes.description: Crane up over the flats; the diagram shows the summary card. Title card at 65.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Let’s slow everything down. This gold ribbon is a path: a map $f$ from the interval $I = [0, 1]$ into the flats.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Slide $s$ from 0 to 1, and $f(s)$ runs along the ribbon from one post to the other.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Now let the tide move it. At each time $t$ there’s a new path, $fₜ$. Here are a few frames.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Stack every frame and you get one map $F(s, t)$ on the square $I × I$: $s$ along the ribbon, $t$ through time. Each row of the square is one frame.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: So a homotopy is the whole movie — not just the first and last picture.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: The Tide Glass scrubs that movie. Press 3 to hold it; Z and X — or the wheel — move $t$ back and forth.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Watch the faint ghosts either side: in a real homotopy, neighbouring frames are always close together.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: And the posts? The ribbon’s ends never move, in any frame: $F(0, t) = a$ and $F(1, t) = b$ for every $t$.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: That’s a homotopy relative to $A$ — $rel A$ — where $A$ is the set of points on the ribbon that are pinned in place.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Your Spool makes homotopies by hand. Press 2, walk up to the ribbon and click to grab it.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Walk, and the ribbon follows. Every step is a new frame, so the movie stays continuous.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Click beside a stake to let go: the ribbon hooks on, and that point joins $A$ — one more point that stays put.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Three things break a homotopy. A cut: the ribbon has to stay in one piece.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: A jump: no frame can leap away from the one before.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: And crossing water: every frame has to stay on the flats.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: So: a homotopy is a continuous movie of paths, and $rel A$ means the pinned points stay put. That’s all the shrines ask.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: Bend, don’t break. Got it.

videos.title: Same Shape
videos.plays: After the 0-3 intro, before play starts; replayable from the level's “How it works” button
videos.synopsis: Homotopy equivalence, slowly: explicit maps f (eight → theta) and g (theta → eight, collapsing the bar), drawn as gold threads; a point's round trip lands near home and slides back (g∘f ≃ 1). Then the quick proof the level uses — one reef that deformation retracts onto both — contractibility, and the controls.

scenes.title: Same shape?
scenes.description: A figure-eight and a theta side by side in gold. The diagram asks X ≟ Y.

scenes.title: Maps both ways
scenes.description: Gold threads draw f from the eight to the theta, then g back. The diagram shows X ⇄ Y with f and g.

scenes.title: Round trips slide home
scenes.description: A bead travels p → f(p) → g(f(p)) and slides back to p along the eight. The diagram: g∘f ≃ 1, f∘g ≃ 1.

scenes.title: One reef, two spines
scenes.description: A two-hole reef slides onto a figure-eight, grows back, and slides onto a theta. The diagram: Z deformation retracts onto X and onto Y, so X ≃ Y.

scenes.title: Contractible
scenes.description: A solid reef slides onto a point; a loop around a ring's hole catches.

scenes.title: How to play
scenes.description: Controls for spines and Slide; Mirror spawn and their reflections.

scenes.title: Summary
scenes.description: Summary card; title card at 66.5.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Two reefs: a figure-eight and a theta. They look different. Are they the same shape?

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: In topology, “same shape” means something precise — maps both ways that can be undone, up to sliding.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Start with a map f from the eight to the theta: each loop of the eight goes once around one loop of the theta.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: The crossing goes to the middle of the bar. Each gold thread joins a point to where f sends it.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: And a map g back: squash the theta’s bar to the crossing, and wrap each side around a loop of the eight.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Now follow one point there and back: across to the theta by f, then home by g.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: It doesn’t land exactly where it started…

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: No — but it slides home along the eight. g after f is homotopic to the identity.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: When both round trips slide home, f is a homotopy equivalence: X and Y are the same shape.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: There’s a quicker way to prove it: find one reef that slides onto both.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: This reef deforms onto the eight… and onto the theta. Same shape.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: A reef that slides onto a single point is contractible: the same shape as a point.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: A loop around a hole catches. Proving the ring isn’t contractible has to wait for World 1.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: To prove a reef: Spool (2), click to start the thread, walk it through the beacons, click to stop — then Slide.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: And Mirror spawn come in pairs. Lash the solid one; the flickering one is only a reflection.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: Same shape, different look. Let’s open that gate.

videos.title: Built from Cells
videos.plays: After the 0-4 intro, before play starts; replayable from the level's “How it works” button
videos.synopsis: Cell complexes, slowly: skeletons X⁰ ⊂ X¹ ⊂ X²; the sphere as a point and a disk; the torus as a square glued along a b a⁻¹ b⁻¹ (folded live); the projective plane along a a (crossing itself in 3D); χ; then Gyroid works a furnace to show the controls.

scenes.title: Built in stages
scenes.description: A point appears; two loops grow out of it and back (edges glued at both ends); a disk fills one loop. The diagram lists X⁰ ⊂ X¹ ⊂ X².

scenes.title: The sphere
scenes.description: A flat disk curls up as its whole rim is drawn to one point: a sphere. Diagram: e⁰ ∪ e² = S².

scenes.title: The torus
scenes.description: A square with arrowed edges a, b rolls into a tube (a meets a), then bends into a ring (b meets b). Diagram: a b a⁻¹ b⁻¹.

scenes.title: Arrows matter
scenes.description: A disk whose rim runs round loop a twice, the same way: it folds into a surface that passes through itself — the projective plane.

scenes.title: χ
scenes.description: Counting cells: points − edges + disks for each build.

scenes.title: At the furnace
scenes.description: Gyroid steps onto a furnace, clicks to forge the point, walks the track out and back to forge edge a, walks it again to write a, and clicks to press a disk along a (a hemisphere folds above the press).

scenes.title: Summary
scenes.description: The torus again; the summary card.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Everything in the Foundry is built in stages. First, points — the 0-cells.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Then edges, glued on by their two ends. Glue both ends to the same point and the edge becomes a loop.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Then disks, glued along loops. Each stage sits inside the next.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: The simplest sphere: one point, and one disk whose entire rim is crushed onto that point.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: Like pulling the drawstring on a bag until the opening's gone.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: The torus: one point, two loops $a$ and $b$, and one square disk. Its rim is glued along $a b a⁻¹ b⁻¹$.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Watch matching arrows meet: the two a-sides glue into a tube, then the two b-sides bend the tube round into a ring.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Now one loop, $a$, and a disk whose rim goes round $a$ twice — the same way both times.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: There’s no room in our space to do that without the disk passing through itself. That’s the projective plane.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: And a count: points minus edges plus disks. That’s χ, the Euler characteristic.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Build the same place two different ways and χ comes out the same — though proving that waits for World 2.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Here's how it works at a furnace. Watch Gyroid.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Click the furnace with the Cell-Smith: that's the point.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Walk out along the track, round its loop and back onto the furnace: an edge, $a$ — a loop at the point.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Walk it again, the way its arrows point. That writes $a$ on the disk's rim — see “walked” on the panel.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Then click the furnace: the press glues a disk along $a$. A bowl — a hemisphere.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: And lash the Unglues — if one tears an edge, walk that track again.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: Points, edges, disks. Let's build.

videos.title: New Spaces from Old
videos.plays: After the 0-5 intro, before play starts; replayable from the level's “How it works” button
videos.synopsis: Operations on spaces, slowly: the cone (a ring's hole fills and every loop slides to the tip); the suspension (two points → a circle → a sphere); the wedge (two rings touch at one point); the product (a small ring swept round a big one: a torus, with a cell for each pair of cells); the quotient (a disk's rim collapsed: a sphere); then the works' controls.

scenes.title: The cone
scenes.description: A glowing ring; its tip rises and pulls it into a cone. A loop on the rim slides up the cone and vanishes at the tip. Diagram: CX, X's cells plus one on each plus the tip; χ = 1.

scenes.title: The suspension
scenes.description: Two points sprout arcs to a tip above and below: a circle. The circle grows a double cone that rounds into a sphere. Diagram: S(S⁰) = S¹, S(S¹) = S².

scenes.title: The wedge
scenes.description: Two rings glide together until they touch at one point: a figure-eight. Diagram: X ∨ Y, cells add, minus one point.

scenes.title: The product
scenes.description: A small ring travels round a big one, sweeping out a torus. Diagram: the four pairs of cells, 1 + 2 + 1.

scenes.title: The quotient
scenes.description: A disk's rim is drawn to one point and it closes into a sphere. Diagram: D²/∂D² = S²; collapsing something contractible keeps the shape.

scenes.title: How to play
scenes.description: The works' controls: pick up, feed, choose the operation, take the result off the shelf, pull plugs.

scenes.title: Summary
scenes.description: Cone, suspension, wedge, product, quotient — and the cells each adds.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: A cone: take a space and join every one of its points to a single new tip.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Cone a ring and the hole fills in. Any loop on it can slide up to the tip and shrink away — a cone always shrinks to its tip.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: A suspension uses two tips, one above and one below. Suspend two points and you get two arcs: a circle.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Suspend the circle and you get a double cone, which is a sphere. Each suspension climbs one dimension.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: A wedge glues two spaces together at a single point. Two rings make a figure-eight.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: A product: every point of one space paired with every point of the other. A ring times a ring, swept round, is a torus.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Its cells come in pairs: point with point, point with edge, edge with point, edge with edge. That's one point, two edges and one disk.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: A quotient collapses part of a space to a single point. Collapse a disk's rim and it closes up into a sphere.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: The rim was a loop, so the shape changed. Collapse something that shrinks to a point and the shape stays the same.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: At each works: click a pedestal to pick up a copy of its space, then click the machine to feed it in.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: New spaces land on the shelf, and you can carry them back in. Lash the Coners. If one plugs a pedestal, click it to pull the plug.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: Cone, suspend, wedge, multiply, collapse. Got it.

videos.title: Felling Trees
videos.plays: After the 0-6 intro, before play starts; replayable from the level's “How it works” button
videos.synopsis: Felling trees, slowly: a tree (no cycle) has n − 1 edges and collapses to a point safely; a graph with a cycle — a triangle with a tail — gets a spanning tree marked (n − 1 edges touching every node, the edge that would close the cycle refused), and felling it leaves the unmarked edge as a loop round the surviving hole; collapsing the cycle too kills the hole; χ = nodes − edges and petals = 1 − χ; then the Spool and Cell-Smith controls. Uses both names: nodes (platforms) and edges (walkways).

scenes.title: A tree
scenes.description: A tree of 4 nodes and 3 edges. Gyroid marks each edge amber (n − 1 = 3), then fells it: every node slides into one — a point.

scenes.title: A cycle
scenes.description: A triangle with a tail: 4 nodes, 4 edges. The triangle's three edges glow pink — a cycle — round a dark disk labelled 'hole'.

scenes.title: A spanning tree
scenes.description: Gyroid marks the tail and two sides of the triangle: 3 = n − 1 edges, every node reached. He tries the third side; it flashes red, refused — it would close the cycle.

scenes.title: Fell
scenes.description: The marked tree folds into one node; the unmarked side rounds out into a loop at that node, the hole carried inside it.

scenes.title: The wrong cut
scenes.description: The same graph with all four edges marked violet, cycle included; it collapses to a point and the hole shrinks to nothing.

scenes.title: χ
scenes.description: The petal again; diagram: tree 4 − 3 = 1 → no petals, cycle 4 − 4 = 0 → one petal, petals = 1 − χ.

scenes.title: How to play
scenes.description: Spool marks edges, cycle-closing edges refused; Cell-Smith clicks any node to fell; lash Loop-biters.

scenes.title: Summary
scenes.description: Every connected graph is a bouquet of 1 − χ circles.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: A graph is made of nodes — the platforms — joined by edges — the walkways. This one is a tree: it has no cycles.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: A tree on $n$ nodes always has exactly $n − 1$ edges. Here: 4 nodes, 3 edges. Gyroid marks them all.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Now he fells it: every edge shrinks, every node slides into one. A tree has no hole in it, so nothing is lost — it’s just a point.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: This graph has a cycle: the triangle. Follow its three edges and you come back where you started.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: A cycle goes round a hole. That hole is what makes this space more than a point, and we must not lose it.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: So we don’t fell everything. Gyroid marks a spanning tree: edges that reach every node, never closing a cycle. That takes $n − 1 = 3$ edges.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: The third side of the triangle? Refused. Marking it would close the cycle, and a cycle isn’t a tree.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Every node is touched, no cycle is closed. That’s a spanning tree.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Fell it. The tree shrinks into one node — safe, because a tree has no hole.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: The edge he didn’t mark now starts and ends at that one node: it’s a loop, a petal. The hole is still inside it.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Now the wrong cut: mark every edge, the cycle too, and squash it all.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Everything goes to a point, and the hole dies with it. That’s a different space — Null’s move.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Count nodes minus edges: that’s $χ$. The tree: $4 − 3 = 1$. The cycle graph: $4 − 4 = 0$.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Felling never changes $χ$, and the petals you end with number $1 − χ$.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: On the decks: hold the Spool and click edges to mark a spanning tree. An edge that would close a cycle is refused.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: When the tree reaches every node, take the Cell-Smith and click any node to fell onto it. And lash those Loop-biters.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: Mark a tree, keep the cycles. Timber!

videos.title: One Cell at a Time
videos.plays: After the 0-B intro; replayable from the level's “How it works” button
videos.synopsis: The homotopy extension property, slowly: X × I as space × time; A's given motion as teal columns; extending over a free point (it stays put) and an edge (it stretches between its ends); a disk refused until its whole rim moves; why it always works (Dⁿ × I retracts onto its floor and walls); controls.

scenes.title: Space × time
scenes.description: An edge on the cylinder floor; its left end's motion rises as a teal column.

scenes.title: Extend
scenes.description: The right point's column rises straight; then the edge's sheet stretches between the two columns.

scenes.title: Boundary first
scenes.description: A square with a disk: the disk is refused (its rim flashes red); points, then edges fill; then the disk's column.

scenes.title: Why it works
scenes.description: Diagram: projecting Dⁿ × I from a point above lands it on its floor and walls.

scenes.title: How to play
scenes.description: Click glowing cells; refused cells show what's missing.

scenes.title: Summary
scenes.description: Every CW pair has the homotopy extension property.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: The cylinder's floor is a space, X. Going up the cylinder is time.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Part of the floor, A, already has a motion chosen for it. Here it's the left point, drifting as time goes up.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: To extend the motion, start with the free point. It only has to start in the right place, so it can just stay put.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Now both ends of the edge are decided. The edge's column simply stretches between them.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: A disk is different. Its column has a floor and walls, and the walls are its rim's columns. Until those are decided, it's refused.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: So go in order of dimension: points, then the edges around the disk, then the disk itself.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Why does the disk's column always fill? A box, disk times time, can be squashed onto just its floor and walls.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Shine a light from a point above it: every point of the box lands on the floor or a wall.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: In the Cylinder Works: click a glowing cell on the floor to raise its column.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: If its boundary isn't decided yet, the missing cells flash red.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: One cell at a time. Got it.

videos.title: The Tide Bends Everything
videos.plays: Before World 0 · Level 2, when Gyroid reaches Tidewarp Flats
videos.synopsis: Past the broken causeway (bridged with the Spool), the tide reshapes Tidewarp Flats every hour. Emmy frames 0-2: a homotopy is a whole continuous movie of maps, and a homotopy 'rel A' keeps some posts fixed throughout. Null offers a cheat — send everything to one point instantly — and Emmy names the difference between a retraction and a deformation.

scenes.title: Bridging the gap
scenes.description: The broken causeway from Twin Lagoons. Gyroid runs a gold Spool thread across the gap; it firms into a spine and the causeway knits along it. Beyond: wide wet tidal flats.

scenes.title: The tide
scenes.description: On the flats, glowing gold ribbon paths lie between stone posts. The tide rolls in and every ribbon bends smoothly into a new shape — ghost copies trace the motion. One middle post stays lit and every ribbon passes through it the whole time.

scenes.title: Null's shortcut
scenes.description: A violet flash: Count Null's image hangs over the water. With a flick he sends a ribbon to a single point — no motion in between, it simply snaps there. Sparks of violet where it tore.

scenes.title: Emmy's answer
scenes.description: Emmy kneels by a ribbon and slows the tide with a gesture; the ribbon bends frame by frame, the fixed post never moving. Gyroid lays a hand on the post.

scenes.title: Title
scenes.description: Wide over the flats as the tide turns. Title card at 28: “World 0 · Level 2 — Bend, Don't Break”.

captions.speaker: Narrator
captions.text: The Spool bridged the broken causeway. Beyond it, the tide had its own ideas.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Tidewarp Flats. Every hour the tide reshapes every path out here — continuously, one moment flowing into the next.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: That whole movie of shapes is a homotopy.

captions.speaker: Count Null
captions.text: Why wait for the tide? I can send every path to one point. Instantly.

captions.speaker: Count Null
captions.text: Every space retracts to a point, courier.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: A retraction can be one snap. A deformation is the whole movie — every frame in between — and with a pool in the way, no such movie exists.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: And these posts never move while the tide works?

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: That's a homotopy $rel$ those posts: they stay still the whole time.
